claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977 (Turner statement and Appendix B); Rockefeller Commission report, June 1975; Ford signing statement, 12 October 1976; Olson v. United States, D.D.C., 17 July 2013, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The four opened records do not agree. The Rockefeller Commission and President Ford give a tenth floor window; the Church Committee text in the 1977 Senate print gives a tenth story window of the Statler Hotel and the death as 27 November 1953; Ford and the 2012 complaint give 28 November; the complaint gives thirteen stories at 2:30 a.m. The CIA told the Senate in 1977 that he 'leaped to his death from a hotel room window in New York City about a week after having unwittingly consumed LSD'.

claims.sourceText: Memorandum for the DDCI, 22 June 1977, Appendix B of the Project MKULTRA joint hearing, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The same memorandum records that the case was in litigation and sets the order of notification: 'The MARKS case is in litigation and we are committed to advise Mr. Marks of the existence of these files shortly, and to deliver the releasable material to his attorneys by 31 July.' Its recommended actions are to release sanitized material to his attorneys as required by FOIA litigation and to 'Inform the Senate Select Committee of the existence of the recently located records prior to informing Mr. Marks' attorneys.'

Brandwein, Director, Office of Technical Service, Appendix B of the Project MKULTRA joint hearing, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The Agency's own memorandum names the request and the mechanism: 'As a result of John Marks FOIA request (F-76-374), all of the MKULTRA material in OTS possession was reviewed for possible release to him. Following that review, the OTS material in the Retired Records Center was searched. It was during that latter search that the subproject files were located among the retired records of the OTS Budget and Fiscal Section.'

claims.sourceText: Opening statement, Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The Senate said the same thing without the name: 'Then one individual, through a Freedom of Information request, accomplished what two U.S. Senate committees could not. He spurred the agency into finding additional records pertaining to the CIA's program of experimentation with human subjects.'

claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, Appendix B, section 2, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The programme's lineage is in the 1977 Senate print: 'The earliest of the CIA's major programs involving the use of chemical and biological agents, Project BLUEBIRD, was approved by the Director in 1950 ... In August 1951, the project was renamed ARTICHOKE.' Responsibility passed in 1952 from the Office of Scientific Intelligence to the Inspection and Security Office, which the same text reads as a shift from studying hostile powers to using the techniques.

claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, opening statement and testimony of Admiral Turner, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The recovered material covers 149 numbered subprojects plus two boxes of audit reports and financial statements from cut-out funding mechanisms and 33 further subprojects unrelated to behavioural work. Turner told the committee the new identities were 'the names of 185 nongovernment researchers and assistants' and 'names of 80 institutions', comprising 44 colleges or universities, 15 research foundations or chemical or pharmaceutical companies, 12 hospitals or clinics and 3 penal institutions. The hearing's own opening statement gives a different figure, 'Eighty-six universities or institutions were involved.'

claims.sourceText: Report of Inspection of MKULTRA, 26 July 1963, p. 14, quoted in the prepared statement of Admiral Stansfield Turner, Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The same survey records the programme's own record-keeping practice: 'Present practice is to maintain no records of the planning and approval of test programs.' The Director of Central Intelligence quoted that sentence back to the Senate in 1977 as part of the reason so little was known even before the files were destroyed.

claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA, The CIA's Program of Research in Behavioral Modification, joint hearing, 3 August 1977, Appendix B, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The Church Committee text reprinted in the hearing print records the destruction and the chain behind it: 'In January 1973, MKULTRA records were destroyed by Technical Services Division personnel acting on the verbal orders of Dr. Sidney Gottlieb, Chief of TSD. Dr. Gottlieb has testified, and former Director Helms has confirmed, that in ordering the records destroyed, Dr. Gottlieb was carrying out the verbal order of then DCI Helms.'

claims.sourceText: Prepared statement of Admiral Stansfield Turner, Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: The surviving records are finance folders and they survived by accident. DCI Stansfield Turner reported 'our recent discovery of seven boxes of documents related to Project MKULTRA', found at the Retired Records Center because the Budget and Fiscal Section had sent them there in 1970 in what the statement calls a departure from normal procedure whose reason 'is not known'. As a result 'the material escaped retrieval and destruction in 1973 ... as well as discovery in 1975'.

claims.sourceText: Memorandum for the Deputy Director of Central Intelligence, 'Request for Guidance on Handling Recently Located MKULTRA Material', 22 June 1977, from David S. Brandwein, Director, Office of Technical Service, Appendix B of the Project MKULTRA joint hearing, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: A CIA memorandum of 22 June 1977 reprinted in the hearing print explains why the 1973 searches missed the finance folders: 'Because Dr. Gottlieb retrieved and destroyed all the MKULTRA documents he was able to locate, it is not surprising that the earlier search for MKULTRA documents, directed at areas where they were most likely to be found, was unsuccessful.'

claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, Appendix B, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: He is one of the two officers named as running the experiment that killed Frank Olson: 'The drug had been placed in the bottle by a CIA officer, Dr. Robert Lashbrook, as part of an experiment he and Dr. Sidney Gottlieb performed at a meeting of Army and CIA scientists.' The same text records that neither the Chief of TSS nor the Deputy Director for Plans specifically authorized that experiment.

claims.sourceText: Project MKULTRA joint hearing, 3 August 1977, Appendix B, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/sites/default/files/hearings/95mkultra.pdf
claims.text: He gave the destruction order. 'In January 1973, MKULTRA records were destroyed by Technical Services Division personnel acting on the verbal orders of Dr. Sidney Gottlieb, Chief of TSD. Dr. Gottlieb has testified, and former Director Helms has confirmed, that in ordering the records destroyed, Dr. Gottlieb was carrying out the verbal order of then DCI Helms.'

edges.label: CIA interrogation-team programme, 1950 to 1951, then ARTICHOKE
edges.note: Proposed by the Chief of the Agency's Inspection and Security Staff for the operational support of OSO and OPC, and renamed ARTICHOKE in August 1951 per the Church Committee text reprinted in the 1977 Senate print.

edges.label: The 1950 predecessor of the 1953 programme
edges.note: Appendix B of the 1977 print treats BLUEBIRD/ARTICHOKE and MKULTRA as successive sections of one lineage of CIA chemical and biological behavioural work, the first approved in 1950 and the second in April 1953.

edges.label: Records destroyed January 1973; a misfiled finance set survived
edges.note: The destruction is recorded in the 1977 hearing print, and so is the accident that defeated it: finance folders sent to the Retired Records Center in 1970 outside normal procedure were missed in 1973 and again in 1975 and found in 1977.

a.label: Senate Select Committee to Study Governmental Operations with Respect to Intelligence Activities (Church Committee)

edges.label: Investigated MKULTRA in 1975 without the finance file
edges.note: Turner's 1977 statement records that the 1975 searches covered the active and retired records of every branch thought likely to hold MKULTRA papers but not the Budget and Fiscal Section's retired holdings, so the Church Committee investigated the programme without the seven boxes.

edges.label: Ordered the destruction of the MKULTRA files, January 1973
edges.note: The 1977 CIA memorandum reprinted in the hearing print says he retrieved and destroyed all the MKULTRA documents he was able to locate, which is why the 1973 and 1975 searches found nothing.
